events.title: First penal settlement
hints: A remote island was settled a few weeks after the First Fleet reached the mainland.
Convicts cleared land and cut pine and flax.
events.summary: Within weeks of the First Fleet landing at Sydney in 1788, convicts and marines were sent to settle the island, intended as a supply station of timber and flax. The settlement proved difficult and was evacuated in 1814.

events.title: Second penal settlement
hints: The island was reopened in 1825 as a place of punishment for repeat offenders.
Floggings and harsh discipline became infamous.
Mutinies in the 1840s led to mass executions.
events.summary: Britain reopened the island in 1825 as a place of secondary punishment for convicts who had re-offended in the Australian colonies. It became notorious for harsh discipline, with floggings and chain gangs, and convict mutinies in the 1840s ended in executions. The settlement closed in 1855.
